issues.body: In `build_report`, an absent case ID or encoding synthesizes status `missing`, then the `skipped-no-odre`/`missing` branch records `verdict = "skipped"`. However, report status depends only on `odre_meta.status`, so when ODRE is present the report remains `complete`; the missing result is excluded from `comparable`, and `main` exits 0 if the remaining divergences are classified. This contradicts the schema's `complete` contract (every case has a real verdict) and allows a truncated/corrupt `odre-decisions.json` to produce a misleading PASS and agreement rate. The self-test does not exercise this path.
issues.fix_hint: When ODRE metadata says `present`, treat any missing case, missing encoding, duplicate case ID, or unexpected case ID as an input/completeness error and exit nonzero before computing agreement. Validate exact case-ID and encoding coverage in both directions. Add a self-test that deletes one case/encoding result and proves the lane fails rather than emitting a complete report.
issues.title: Missing ODRE results are silently treated as skips in a complete run

issues.body: `main` checks only that the static ledger and capability table agree with each other. It never compares `decisions["odre"]["version"]` to their pinned version. `odre_adapter.py` permits any importable `pyodre` from `ODRE_PYTHON` and even records `unknown` on metadata failure, yet the classifier then applies source-read rules specifically attributed to pyodre 1.0.6 and reports the system as the pinned implementation. A different installed release can therefore be scored and have its divergences excused using stale 1.0.6 assumptions.
issues.fix_hint: For a present ODRE installation, require the observed package version to equal the ledger/capability pin before running or classifying; reject `unknown` and mismatches with a nonzero input/incomplete exit. Add a self-test for a mismatched observed version. If non-pinned runs are intentionally supported, they must not use the pinned capability/divergence ledger or make pinned-version claims.
issues.title: The pinned ODRE implementation version is not enforced

verdict.summary: The lane is not fail-closed for incomplete ODRE output. Although the schema and report status define `complete` as every case having a real verdict, a missing case/encoding result is converted to `skipped`, excluded from agreement tallies, and still permits status `complete` and exit 0. This can publish a PASS/agreement figure from only a subset of the exported corpus. Runtime enforcement of the claimed ODRE version pin is also missing: the installed version is recorded but never checked against 1.0.6 before applying version-specific capability and divergence rules.
